title: Sell Mineral Rights in Wildrose, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Wildrose, ND
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Wildrose, ND in Williams County? Core Bakken acreage in a quiet corner of the play. Get a fair, honest offer.
heroLead: Wildrose sits in the northern part of Williams County, quiet even by the standards of a rural oil county, and the mineral interests here don't get talked about the way Williston or Tioga do.
intro: That relative quiet doesn't mean there's nothing under the ground. Williams County's core Bakken acreage extends up through this part of the county, and families who inherited a fraction of an interest near Wildrose sometimes find it's worth considerably more than they assumed based on how little attention the area gets.

sections.heading: Northern Williams County's real production history
paragraphs: Horizontal Bakken development has reached well into the northern part of the county over the years, and Wildrose-area tracts have generally participated in that even without much individual name recognition. We check the state well index against your specific legal description before saying what we think it's worth.

sections.heading: Getting a clear picture of an inherited interest
paragraphs: If you inherited a Wildrose-area interest and have no idea what it's actually producing or whether it's even still leased, we start by pulling the Williams County Recorder's file and the state's well records to build a clear picture before we ever talk about buying.

sections.heading: Why we treat quiet-corner tracts with the same care
paragraphs: It would be easy to give a Wildrose owner a rushed, generic answer since the area doesn't draw the attention Williston does. We don't do that. We check the actual wells and spacing units tied to your legal description with the same care we'd give a tract in the busiest part of the county.
That's part of why our offers tend to hold up when compared against other buyers who skip that step.

faqs.question: Wildrose doesn't come up much in Bakken news. Is our interest still worth checking?
faqs.answer: Yes, northern Williams County has seen real development even without the same attention as Williston or Tioga. It's worth having us check your specific tract.

faqs.question: We inherited this and have no records at all. Where do you even start?
faqs.answer: With whatever name or address you have connected to the property, we can search the Williams County Recorder's records to identify the interest and its history.

faqs.question: Is it possible our interest isn't leased at all right now?
faqs.answer: Yes, that happens, and we can still make an offer on unleased minerals, it just changes how we approach the valuation.

faqs.question: Will you actually check well data specific to our tract, or just give a general county estimate?
faqs.answer: We always check your specific legal description against the state's well index. A general county number isn't something we're willing to offer as a real price.
